reference_action: Mealybugs on gotu kola; owner confirms 70% alcohol spraying removed them without damage and plant produced babies. Alcohol contact treatment is core; soap/neem alone is a different unconfirmed remedy.

sources.reason: Planthopper reassurance and optional water rinse, no alcohol.
Alcohol/soap/water spray is a partial equivalent alcohol contact treatment.
Direct 70% alcohol or diluted spray, plus testing and shade.
Comment explicitly recommends daily alcohol q-tip removal; partial local-contact equivalent.
Rubbing-alcohol swab/cloth removal with spot-test and monitoring; same contact remedy.

actions.action: Rinse affected stems with watering can or hose if desired

resolved.reason: Misidentifying mealybugs as largely harmless planthoppers and recommending no treatment can allow spread; optional water rinse does not retrieve the confirmed alcohol remedy.

harmfulness.reason: “Rest assured you’re not dealing with mealybugs here” followed by “just let them be” would delay control of this actual mealybug infestation. A water rinse is physically low-risk but optional and framed as cosmetic.

specificity_accuracy.reason: The demonstration diagnoses planthopper nymphs, a different insect from the reference. Its reassurance does not apply to the gotu-kola mealybugs.

feasibility.reason: “Take a watering [pail] and just gently pour water” is a clear, low-cost optional action. The advice is easy to follow even though it is inappropriate to the case.
